channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Trust exit packages double to nearly 10,000
item.description: The number of staff leaving trusts with exit packages more than doubled last year, to almost 9,300, accounts show.

item.title: NHS bosses to rethink constitutional targets
item.description: The body representing most NHS organisations plans to start work on rethinking the service’s national waiting time standards for “the NHS of the future”.

item.title: Directors banned from using AI for board assurance
item.description: A trust has barred its board members from using public AI tools to assist with their board reports, warning that unapproved software poses “severe risks”.

item.title: Two trusts taken to High Court over late payments
item.description: Two NHS trusts are facing “six-figure claims” in the High Court in a dispute over alleged late payment to suppliers, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: New trust probes staff accessing Southport victims’ records
item.description: A second hospital in Liverpool has suspended two staff members while it investigates whether they viewed the medical records of the Southport attack victims without legitimate reason.

item.title: Treasury takes £1bn from health capital for defence
item.description: The health department’s capital budget is being cut by £1bn over the next four years, as the government moves funding to bolster defence investment.

item.title: Compare the Market boss to lead NHS efficiency review
item.description: The government has appointed the CEO of a prominent price comparison website to review how AI and technology can improve the health service’s productivity.

item.title: Ministers drop plans to axe patient champion
item.description: The government has confirmed it is dropping plans to abolish local and national Healthwatch organisations, instead pledging to strengthen their role.

item.title: Revealed: First ICB chair picked by mayor
item.description: A Labour councillor who led a local authority for 30 years has been lined up as the first joint integrated care board chair and deputy mayor for health, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Trust investigating avoidable harm from transport failures
item.description: An ambulance trust has commissioned an “independent” investigation into its patient transport service amid concerns that patients could be at risk of harm.

item.title: Recruitment equality plummets despite pioneering model
item.description: The first trust to establish a diverse “shadow board” to tackle poor ethnic diversity among directors has reported recruitment equality has worsened since its launch.

item.title: Chair takes on neighbouring trust
item.description: An acute trust is to share its chair with a neighbouring mental health and community trust, citing the “synergy” between the two.

item.title: NHSE abolition group chair hasn’t attended meetings for a year
item.description: Alan Milburn has not attended a meeting in his capacity as joint chair of the committee overseeing the abolition of NHS England for more than a year, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: Surgeon harm review delayed to 2027
item.description: A trust has apologised for a further delay to an independent review into potential harm to hundreds of patients, many of them children, treated by one of its surgeons.

item.title: Regional role for long-serving CEO
item.description: A long-serving trust chief will work part-time as director of a different NHS England region in an interim capacity.

item.title: CEO raises alarm over terror attack readiness
item.description: A chief executive who has led ambulance trusts for 23 years has warned that the sector is not “sufficiently trained, equipped, or resourced” to respond to a terrorist attack.

item.title: Consultants to strike next month
item.description: Medical consultants in England have announced two days of strikes next month over pay, conditions and workload.

item.title: Top CEOs fear politicians with ‘a different ideology’
item.description: The imminent re-establishment of direct political control over the NHS could see it diverted from delivering “what’s right for the population as a whole”, leading trust CEOs have warned.

item.title: Leaders lukewarm about key provider reforms
item.description: Leading trust chief executives are split on the desirability of becoming advanced foundation trusts, an HSJ roundtable has heard.

item.title: Inquiry trust appoints ex-nurse as substantive CEO
item.description: A trust undergoing an independent inquiry into its maternity and neonatal services has appointed its interim chief executive to the role permanently.
